summary.headline: KNR Constructions Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR587.9 crore with 16.4% EBITDA margin, lifted by a ~INR46 crore one-off from a cash-surplus EPC claim.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q1 FY27 revenue was INR587.9 crore, EBITDA INR96.4 crore (16.4% margin) and net profit INR80.7 crore, with standalone revenue INR436.7 crore. Management said the margin is flattered by a one-off of about INR46 crore (INR76 crore revenue less INR30 crore cost); excluding it, EBITDA margin is about 5.5%. Consolidated debt fell to INR1,975 crore from INR2,438 crore, while net debt/equity rose to 0.9 from 0.49 and working capital days rose to 133 from 78. Order book is INR15,234 crore including the two new HAM projects and the Kusmunda mining project, and management guided FY27 revenue to INR2,200-2,300 crore.

financial_highlights.value: About INR46 crore net (INR76 crore revenue less INR30 crore expense) from cash-surplus EPC claim on KNR Palani sale; margin ex one-off about 5.5%

segments.name: HAM (Hybrid Annuity Model)
segments.commentary: About 70% of Q1 revenue. HAM physical progress at 30 June 2026: Ramanattukara-Valanchery and Valanchery-Kappirikkad 100%, Magadi-Somwarpet ~91.35%, Marripudi-Somavarappadu ~86.03%, Mysore-Kushalnagara Package 4 ~20%, Package 5 ~18.28%.

segments.name: Irrigation
segments.commentary: About 3% of Q1 revenue. Irrigation order book INR1,685 crore as of June, of which about INR825 crore is unbilled-but-recognised; FY27 irrigation revenue guided at about INR200 crore.

segments.name: Water pipeline
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue only INR7 crore. Order book about INR830 crore, back-to-back, with FY27 target INR300-400 crore.

segments.name: Mining (Kusmunda, Chhattisgarh)
segments.commentary: Letter of acceptance from SECL with JV partner Sushee Infra; total value INR3,361 crore excl. GST over eight years, with KNR taking 100% EPC back-to-back. FY27 revenue guided at about INR150 crore; FY28 about INR400 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue INR2,200-2,300 crore (10-15% above FY26's ~INR2,000 crore) with EBITDA margin 8-9%; FY28 revenue above INR3,000 crore at 11-12% EBITDA margin, per management.
Q3 and Q4 FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 11-12%, as HAM and mining execution starts; Q1 and Q2 margins said to be similar to Q1.
FY29 EBITDA margin guided at about 8-9% on average, per management's answer to an analyst.
FY27 order inflow target INR8,000-10,000 crore (NHAI, irrigation and state government works); order book INR15,234 crore including HAM and mining, with the non-mining book executable in 3-3.5 years.
Standalone FY27 capex INR350-400 crore, mainly mining; Kusmunda equipment spend INR400-450 crore this year.

Telangana irrigation receivables about INR1,300 crore (Package 4); total irrigation receivables about INR1,450 crore. Management expects INR400-500 crore collection in FY27 under proposed instalments.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex was about INR14 crore; Kusmunda mining start (appointed date) expected first or second week of September 2026 after haul-road widening, with 100-tonne dumpers due by end-November.

Kusmunda equipment requirement about INR500-600 crore (surface miners, dumpers, excavators, dozers, graders); management said INR200-250 crore of orders were already placed. Surface miners cost about INR13 crore each, four needed initially.

Banhardih (Jharkhand) mine awaiting forest stage-two clearance and land acquisition, expected to take 8-10 months more; equipment spend INR300-400 crore; FY27 capex contribution about INR200 crore per management.
Two new HAM projects (Chennai ECR and Telangana Mahabubnagar) expected to start in Q3 FY27; further equity of about INR510 crore needed for these projects.
Existing HAM equity: INR595 crore invested out of INR805 crore revised requirement; INR210 crore balance to be infused (INR125 crore FY27, INR85 crore FY28).
demand_pricing: NHAI awarded about 107 km and executed about 638 km in Q1 FY27; NHAI plans to award 54 projects covering 2,444 km worth INR1.8 lakh crore in FY27.
Union budget allocated about INR3.1 lakh crore to MoRTH, with road capex outlay up about 8%; railways capex INR2.93 lakh crore; Andhra Pradesh railway allocation INR10,134 crore.
Order book split: 38% roads, 11% irrigation, 6% pipeline, 45% mining. Client mix: 71% third party (46% central government, 24% state government, 1% private), 29% captive HAM.

Irrigation Telangana recovery: government discussing instalments of about INR70-90 crore per month against about INR650 crore outstanding, plus an INR700 crore+ revised estimate that needs government sanction (5-6 months).
Unbilled order book about INR1,220 crore (irrigation INR825 crore, roads about INR400 crore); Somavarappadu unexecuted about INR100 crore; HAM debtors INR178 crore.
Management said it is only bidding on selected projects; UPEIDA excluded for lack of greenfield expressway experience; battery energy storage bids were lost earlier, with new bids cautiously pursued.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue is expected in the irrigation, pipeline and mining segments in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Irrigation about INR200 crore in FY27; pipeline INR300-400 crore in FY27; mining about INR150 crore in FY27 (Kusmunda only) and about INR400 crore in FY28, with Banhardih possibly adding about INR500 crore a year if it starts.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a one-off in Q1 EBITDA margin of 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management cited a cash-surplus EPC claim of about INR90 crore (incl. GST) from the KNR Palani sale; net one-off in EBITDA is about INR46 crore (INR76 crore revenue less INR30 crore expense), leaving about 5.5% margin.

qa_highlights.question: What are the mining project economics and IRR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bidding assumed about 6%-plus PAT; mining needs INR500-600 crore equipment for about INR400 crore annual turnover over eight years; detailed EBITDA calculation pending, with buyback arrangements on some dumpers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there no buyback or larger dividend despite low capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a buyback is under consideration and a conclusion meeting is pending; Board to decide, with no amount indicated. Equity commitments for HAM and capex are being reserved meanwhile.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Mysore-Kushalnagara still unexecuted and when will it pick up?
qa_highlights.answer: Land handover was delayed by local protests over service roads; land was handed over about two months ago. Management targets partial COD by December and full completion by April-May 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Telangana irrigation money recoverable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects instalments of about INR600-650 crore over five to six months, with INR400-500 crore in FY27 expected; collection requires continuous follow-up with the government.

risks_watch: Q1 EBITDA margin (15%) includes a one-off; underlying margin about 5.5%, so H2 margin recovery to 11-12% depends on HAM and mining start-up.
Working capital days rose to 133 from 78 and net debt/equity to 0.9 from 0.49, while consolidated debt fell; monitor working-capital release.
Telangana irrigation receivables of about INR1,300 crore (Package 4) with instalment and revised-estimate approvals pending; collection timing uncertain.
Kusmunda start date (September) depends on rains, haul-road widening and delivery of 100-tonne dumpers by November; Banhardih forest clearance pending.
Equity needs of about INR210 crore (existing HAM) plus about INR510 crore (new HAM) against a buyback under consideration.
Awarding slowdown: management said NHAI award activity was subdued in early FY27; order inflow target INR8,000-10,000 crore depends on it.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the medium-term outlook (FY28 above INR3,000 crore) but cautious on near-term timing, repeatedly tying start dates and collections to government approvals, rains and land handovers. Answers on buyback, battery storage and the mining IRR were non-committal and deferred to a future Board decision.
key_quotes: The additional equity requirement of INR210 crores to be infused as INR125 crores and INR85 crores is in FY27 and FY28, respectively.
One-off is, in revenue, it is around INR76 crores and expenditure side also, it is around INR30 crores has been there in expenditure side.
So FY27 will be this. And as far as FY28 is concerned, definitely, that year should be the good year because whatever the projects are there, projects will completely start in FY28.
Yes, sir. Buyback, we are considering, sir. We'll come back on it.
Sir, actually, we have decided to make full rounds and get that at least because that is need of an hour.
